questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The most important / of all my goals / are to/ learn English.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'are to'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Using the **linking verb are** in the part ***'are to' ***violates *subject-verb agreement. *
 
• The subject of the sentence is **singular***** **- the person wants to learn English which is the most important of his goals. *
 
• Hence, we cannot use the **plural linking verb are **with a singular subject. 
 
• Hence, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 
 
• The sentence can be correct by using the **singular linking verb is. **

**Correct sentence__ - ***The most important / of all my goals / **is to**/ learn English.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I wish / I am / the Principal / of the school!
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'I am'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **subjunctive mood.**
 
• The **subjunctive mood** is the verb form used to explore a hypothetical situation (e.g., "If I were you") or to express a wish, a demand, or a suggestion (e.g., "I demand he be present").
 
• **I am **is the normal present tense verb form. It cannot be used for the subjunctive mood. 
 
• Hence, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 
 
• The sentence can be corrected by using **I were.**

**Correct sentence__ - ***I wish / **I were** / the Principal / of the school!*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

We’ll look at / your pet / when you go / on a vacation.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'We'll look at'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in using the **preposition at. **
 
• The **preposition “at”** can be used in multiple contexts, such as telling time or location (*e.g., telling someone to meet “at midnight” or “at the coffee shop”).*
 
• But **at **cannot be used to allude to someone or something. 
 
• Hence, the error lies in **We'll look at **making **option 1 **the correct answer. 
 
• The sentence can made correct using the **preposition after. **

**Correct sentence__ - *****We’ll look after **/ your pet / when you go / on a vacation.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The condition of the house __had been so deteriorated__ from lack of maintenance that nobody wanted to purchase it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'had so deteriorated'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part of the given sentence *'had been so deteriorated' *is an **incorrect tense form**. 
 
• If it wanted to imply the **past perfect continuous tense form **then it should have used *deteriorating *with *had been. *
 
• From the sentence we can conclude that the house had already deteriorated from lack of maintenance. The action occurred and ended in the past. 
 
• So, we need to use the **past perfect tense form**. 
 
• Hence, **had so deteriorated **is the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
 
• Thus, **option 4 **is the correct answer. 

**Correct sentence__ - ***The condition of the house **__had so deteriorated__** from lack of maintenance that nobody wanted to purchase it.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Was deteriorating **is the **past continuous tense form. **
 
• **Was so deteriorated **is incorrect.
